title: The proxy is part of the contract
summary: Review a reverse-proxy config for forwarded headers, websocket upgrades, body limits, and bounded timeouts.

scenario.briefing: The campus web app works for page loads but live updates never connect, large uploads fail at one megabyte, and the app sees every client as the proxy's address. The reverse-proxy config was copied from an API proxy that never handled websockets. Review it and write the corrected contract.

objectives.description: Identify missing upgrade, forwarded, limit, and timeout settings.
Write a proxy config that preserves the client contract.
Explain what a proxy must preserve for the application.

hints: A websocket needs an HTTP/1.1 upgrade handshake.
Forwarded headers tell the app the original host, scheme, and client.
Upload limits are part of the product contract, not a security afterthought.
Bound upstream timeouts and keep the health check meaningful.

misconceptions.description: Assuming a reverse proxy forwards everything unchanged.
misconceptions.feedback: A proxy terminates and rebuilds the request. It must forward upgrade headers, client identity, scheme, and body limits deliberately.

misconceptions.description: Using a very long proxy timeout as a safety margin.
misconceptions.feedback: A long timeout holds connections and hides a stalled upstream. Use a bounded timeout and let the app return an error.

misconceptions.description: Treating forwarded headers as optional metadata.
misconceptions.feedback: Without forwarded headers, logs, rate limits, redirects, and CSRF checks use the proxy as the client and the wrong scheme.

sections.title: The proxy rebuilds the request
sections.body: A reverse proxy accepts a client connection and opens a new one upstream. Anything not forwarded is lost: the client address, the original scheme, the Host header, and the upgrade intent for a websocket.

sections.title: Limits are part of the interface
sections.body: client_max_body_size and proxy_read_timeout decide which requests can succeed. A one-megabyte upload limit turns a product feature into a 413. A ten-minute timeout holds resources when the upstream stalls.

sections.title: Health and observability cross the boundary
sections.body: A health check should exercise the dependency the proxy depends on, and logs should carry the forwarded request id and client address. Otherwise the proxy hides the failure it was meant to expose.

steps.title: Review the copied proxy config
steps.prompt: Select every supported finding and choose a verdict.
hints: Look for the HTTP version and Upgrade headers.
Check the body size and read timeout.
Check whether the original host, scheme, and client are forwarded.
Block the config: websockets, uploads, client identity, and timeouts are all wrong.

artifact.title: campus.conf
artifact.caption: Reverse-proxy server block for the campus web app.

findings.label: The config never enables HTTP/1.1 or forwards Upgrade and Connection for websockets.
The one-megabyte body limit rejects the documented upload feature.
A ten-minute read timeout holds connections when the upstream stalls.
The original host, scheme, and client address are not forwarded.
proxy_pass http:// is always a TLS failure.

verdicts.label: Block until upgrade, limits, headers, and timeouts are correct

steps.explanation: The proxy must forward the websocket upgrade, accept the documented upload size, preserve client and scheme headers, and use a bounded timeout.

steps.title: Write the corrected proxy contract
steps.prompt: Edit proxy.conf. Add a websocket upgrade map, enable HTTP/1.1, forward Upgrade and Connection from the map, forward Host, X-Forwarded-For, and X-Forwarded-Proto, allow a ten-megabyte upload, set a thirty-second upstream read timeout, and add a health location.
hints: Use the map value in the Connection header and set HTTP/1.1.
Raise the body limit to 10m, bound the read timeout to 30s, and add a /health location.

tests.description: The app receives the original host, client, and scheme.

steps.title: What the proxy must preserve
hints: The upstream sees a new connection.
Forwarded headers affect logs, redirects, and rate limits.
A timeout is a resource limit.
Select upgrade, forwarded headers, bounded limits, and health checks; reject proxy transparency.

statements.label: Websocket connections need the HTTP/1.1 Upgrade handshake forwarded.
Forwarded host, scheme, and client headers keep logs and redirects accurate.
Body limits and upstream timeouts are part of the product contract.
A proxy health check should exercise the dependency the app needs.
Forwarded headers are optional metadata with no effect on correctness.
A reverse proxy forwards the original request unchanged.

steps.explanation: A proxy is an active participant. It must preserve the upgrade, client identity, scheme, limits, and health contract.
